times.headline: Market Scales Examined
times.body: A market trader has introduced a second set of scales so customers may check the first. Both give different answers. A third set has been ordered, and the trader hopes to settle the matter by majority vote. Purchasers are advised that a thumb is not a recognised unit of weight.

illustration.alt: A brass balance and iron weights beside baskets of onions and cabbages on a market counter
illustration.caption: Among the market stalls.

times.headline: Bakers Discuss Loaf Standard
times.body: Local bakers met to discuss the proper weight of a loaf. Agreement was reached on the importance of bread, followed by considerable disagreement about everything else. The meeting's sample loaf was eventually used to hold the door open. No customers were injured during the demonstration.

illustration.alt: Loaves, a bread peel and flour beside an old brick bakehouse oven
illustration.caption: The early batch.

times.headline: Public Clock Under Repair
times.body: A public clock has stopped, improving its accuracy on two occasions each day. Its keeper asks residents not to strike the mechanism with sticks. Several residents say this removes the only service it was still providing. Repairs are expected when someone has located the correct spring.

times.headline: Umbrella Ownership Disputed
times.body: Two residents have claimed the same umbrella after yesterday's rain. Both identified the bent spoke and neither recognised the initials on its handle. A third claimant says these are precisely the qualities he remembers. The umbrella remains indoors, where it has caused no further trouble.

times.headline: Carters Seek Clearer Directions
times.body: Carters have asked customers to replace directions such as 'behind the usual barrel' with more lasting landmarks. One delivery spent the morning following a barrel through three streets. Its owner says the barrel was making better progress than the cart and should be consulted about future routes.

times.headline: Guild Noticeboard Repaired
times.body: A guild noticeboard has been strengthened after collapsing under notices concerning its unsafe condition. The repairer has left room for a certificate confirming the work. Members are asked to pin complaints near the bottom, where they will provide additional support rather than create a second hazard.

times.headline: Soup Kitchen Receives Ladles
times.body: A charitable kitchen has received six ladles and no bowls following an appeal for utensils. Volunteers thanked donors and requested that future gifts include something into which soup can be put. A nearby cooper has offered a bucket, subject to agreement about the return of his bucket.

times.headline: River Traffic Reports Delay
times.body: A barge was delayed when its cargo of empty crates shifted and filled the space intended for the crew. The skipper described the load as unusually difficult for something consisting mainly of nothing. Unloading resumed after a plank was found. The river declined to comment on its contribution.

illustration.alt: A cargo barge tied to a timber bollard with thick mooring ropes beside old river warehouses
illustration.caption: At the river wharves.

times.headline: Street Sweeper Appeals for Patience
times.body: A sweeper has asked residents to stop congratulating him by throwing things into the street. He says the gesture is appreciated but creates a misleading impression of demand. A clean stretch of paving lasted eleven minutes yesterday. Several pedestrians stopped to determine what was missing.

illustration.alt: Wet cobbles, a puddle, boots and an umbrella beside an old wooden door
illustration.caption: After the rain.

times.headline: Library Book Returned with Apology
times.body: A borrower has returned a library book accompanied by a lengthy apology for its condition. The apology is in better condition than the book and has been filed separately. Readers are reminded that pressing flowers may damage pages, particularly when the flowers are still in their pot.

times.headline: Watch Requests Clear Statements
times.body: Residents reporting disturbances are asked to distinguish what they saw from what somebody nearby felt must have happened. One recent account grew three suspects during the walk to the Watch. Descriptions of hats remain useful, provided the witness also remembers whether someone was wearing them.

times.headline: New Bench Attracts Debate
times.body: A repaired public bench has prompted complaints that it faces the wrong way. Those facing the street prefer the view behind it; those facing the buildings say the street is more interesting. The carpenter has declined to fit a swivel until someone accepts responsibility for the consequences.

times.headline: Bell-Ringer Issues Correction
times.body: Yesterday's extended ringing announced a stuck rope rather than a civic emergency. The bell-ringer regrets the confusion, though he notes the attendance was excellent. Residents who assembled with buckets may collect them from the usual place. Anyone who assembled with a sandwich need take no further action.

times.headline: Drain Inspection Postponed
times.body: An inspection of a blocked drain was postponed after the blockage appeared to inspect the workmen. No firm conclusion has been reached about what moved. The contractor asks spectators to stop feeding it, as this is unlikely to improve either the drainage or the contractor's willingness to return.

illustration.alt: Wet cobbles, a puddle, boots and an umbrella beside an old wooden door
illustration.caption: After the rain.

times.headline: Mended Shoes Await Owners
times.body: A cobbler is seeking owners for several repaired shoes that have outlasted the customers' interest in collecting them. One pair has now been repaired twice without being worn. The cobbler calls this a promising business arrangement, although it would be improved considerably by payment.

times.headline: Gardeners Debate Competition Rules
times.body: Allotment holders have requested a separate prize for vegetables whose appearance distracts the judges from their weight. One judge favours a covered weighing basket. Another favours retirement. Entries remain open, but growers are asked to describe unusual features on the form without drawing diagrams in the margin.

times.headline: Postal Customers Asked to Label Parcels
times.body: Postal customers are reminded that 'you know who' is an inadequate address unless accompanied by further particulars. A parcel addressed to 'the tall one' has generated considerable discussion. Its sender says the description was accurate at the time and objects to being blamed for subsequent growth.

times.headline: Lamp Oil Deliveries Rescheduled
times.body: Lamp oil deliveries will begin earlier after several rounds continued beyond dusk. Drivers welcomed the change, observing that their customers were in a particularly poor position to see them arrive. Purchasers should keep a clear path to the door and avoid testing the contents with a candle.

times.headline: Washerwomen Report Missing Pegs
times.body: Several washerwomen have reported missing clothes pegs. A nearby child denies operating a lending service and says his waiting list proves nothing. Residents are asked to return borrowed pegs before the wind changes. Payment in buttons will be considered only where the buttons still have a useful future.

times.headline: Lost Property Receives Its Own Box
times.body: A lost-property box has been provided after repeated confusion between lost articles and the desk upon which they were left. The box is plainly labelled. Its lid is already missing. Staff hope this demonstrates public awareness of the service rather than a fundamental weakness in its design.

times.headline: Musicians Agree on Rehearsal Hours
times.body: Neighbours and musicians have agreed that rehearsal should occur during daylight. They have not agreed what constitutes a musician. The arrangement will be reviewed after the next session, preferably by someone living further away. A drummer has requested clarification on whether carrying his instrument counts as practice.

times.headline: Second-Hand Signs Change Hands
times.body: A signwriter is offering previously owned shop signs with minor alterations. Demand for 'Fresh Fish' has proved limited among businesses selling neither. Buyers are urged to inspect spelling before collection. The signwriter says punctuation costs extra because it is the part customers most frequently change their minds about.

times.headline: Rain Gauge Results Questioned
times.body: A gardener's report of unprecedented rainfall has been questioned after a neighbour admitted using the measuring jar to rinse a brush. Both agree the weather has been unpleasant. The jar has been emptied and returned to service under supervision. The brush is said to be making a satisfactory recovery.

times.headline: Clacks Queue Moves Indoors
times.body: Customers awaiting the clacks service may shelter indoors during rain, provided they do not obstruct staff. A customer who shouted his message up the tower has been advised that this is a different service. He disputes the distinction but accepts that the receipt would have been difficult to deliver.

illustration.alt: Clerks with dispatch forms and quills beside a clacks tower with square shutter panels
illustration.caption: Messages across the city.

times.headline: Rope Makers Offer Quayside Repairs
times.body: A rope maker near the river has begun setting aside sound offcuts for small repairs to mooring lines. Bargemen may exchange a damaged length rather than purchase a whole coil. The arrangement started when a delivery boy noticed that several boats were tied with knots chiefly intended to conceal the state of the rope. The maker says his contribution is modest: a boat that stays where it was left is more likely to require rope again. Two neighbouring workshops have offered spare pegs and handles. No one has yet volunteered to improve the river.

illustration.alt: A cargo barge tied to a timber bollard with thick mooring ropes beside old river warehouses
illustration.caption: At the river wharves.

times.headline: Pavers Preserve a Doorstep Route
times.body: Residents and a paving crew have agreed to leave a narrow path through a patch of lifted cobbles so customers can reach a row of shops. The first plan required shoppers to cross a plank, which was immediately purchased by a carpenter who thought it had been put out for sale. Work resumed after its return. A laundress has marked the remaining firm stones with chalk. She asks visitors to follow the marks rather than her washing line, which leads to a quite different appointment. The crew hopes the finished surface will last longer than the argument over it.

illustration.alt: Wet cobbles, a puddle, boots and an umbrella beside an old wooden door
illustration.caption: After the rain.

times.headline: University Supper Card Causes Queue
times.body: A discarded Unseen University supper card attracted a small gathering after a pie seller displayed it beside his own menu. Readers were interested in the number of courses rather than the prices, which were absent. One customer offered to buy the card itself, believing it to be a challenge. The pie seller says he intended only to demonstrate the difference between supper and a pie. He has now removed it from the stall. The card has been returned to its owner, who was reportedly concerned that somebody might mistake it for the complete day's catering.

illustration.alt: A wizard hat, biscuits, teapot and a simple seating plan on an old stone-room table
illustration.caption: From the University desk.

times.headline: Clacks Customers Debate the Comma
times.body: Two merchants have settled an argument over a message ordering barrels after discovering that they had read its punctuation differently. One expected empty barrels; the other had arranged for barrels to be emptied. Both accept that the clacks operator transmitted the words they supplied. The resulting stock has been divided by agreement, with the empty containers going to the buyer who can use them. A clerk has proposed reading messages aloud before submission. His employer welcomed the proposal until the clerk reached the part concerning the value of a little more time.

illustration.alt: Clerks with dispatch forms and quills beside a clacks tower with square shutter panels
illustration.caption: Messages across the city.

times.headline: Tailor Adds Fitting Appointments
times.body: A tailor has introduced longer fitting appointments after customers complained that alterations were being discussed across the shop floor. Dwarf clients seeking a particular cut of coat can now examine samples in private, as can anyone else who prefers a conversation without an audience. The proprietor says the change has reduced returns and arguments about what was originally requested. A new ledger records the customer's words beside each measurement. There is no column for whether a neighbour approves of them. The waiting bench has been moved away from the fitting curtain to encourage this distinction.

times.headline: Shelter Bench Finds Evening Use
times.body: A merchant's disused loading shelter is being used as an evening resting place by porters waiting for work. A stone bench installed for troll visitors has proved popular, and a wooden seat has been added beside it. The owner had first intended to charge for the shade, but found it difficult to measure when a cloud passed over. The benches are consequently free. Users have agreed to keep the doorway clear and leave space for the next shift. A broken stool donated to the project has been respectfully returned to the donor.

times.headline: Opera Programme Names the Repairers
times.body: A printer preparing a small programme for an opera rehearsal has included the names of the people who repaired the scenery. The addition followed a carpenter's complaint that he had held up the palace for most of the second act without receiving a mention. Singers will remain listed first. The carpenter says he was not seeking equal prominence, merely acknowledgement that the palace had no opinion about standing upright. Other backstage workers have asked for their names to be spelt correctly. The printer expects this to require more consultation than the original programme.

illustration.alt: Carpenter tools, ropes and timber braces behind a painted palace set in an opera house
illustration.caption: Behind the scenery.

times.headline: Glass Collector Changes His Round
times.body: A collector of chipped drinking glasses has altered his route to avoid the busiest hours outside the Mended Drum. He says the quieter round produces fewer glasses but a greater proportion of complete ones. Several publicans now leave damaged vessels in a box instead of mixing them with kitchen waste. The collector pays according to the usable material, not the history attached to it. One customer offered an especially interesting history and no glass. The offer was declined. A broom has also been placed beside the box, chiefly for the benefit of those carrying it.

times.headline: Reading Table Welcomes Shift Workers
times.body: A small reading circle has moved its gathering to accommodate workers whose shifts end after the usual meetings. A golem participant suggested choosing the time by asking the people who wished to attend. This proved more effective than the committee's previous method of consulting the clock. Members bring their own reading matter and may listen without speaking. The room's owner has donated a lamp and requests that it be left with enough oil for the cleaner. A debate about whether the first book should be short has already become longer than the proposed book.

times.headline: Bell Schedule Displayed in Writing
times.body: A group of worshippers has begun writing down the bells they hear rather than relying on memory when arranging shared meals. The notes show considerable variety in what residents consider noon. Organisers have therefore chosen a single meeting time and placed it on their own door. They stress that no temple has been asked to change its observances. One elderly visitor says the written notice is useful because it can be consulted after the bell has stopped. The first meal under the new arrangement was served warm, which participants consider a promising result.

times.headline: Rat Catchers Compare Empty Traps
times.body: Two rat catchers have discovered that their best traps were being moved between the same three courtyards by residents seeking quicker service. Both had reported excellent demand and disappointing catches. The traps will now be marked, and householders have agreed to report where they were set. A baker helped arrange the conversation after finding a trap beneath his counter that belonged to neither man. Its owner has since collected it. There is no charge for the meeting, although several participants brought invoices in case the opportunity arose. The rats were unavailable for comment.

times.headline: Workshop Courtyard Shares a Drying Rack
times.body: Neighbours in a busy workshop courtyard have erected a shared drying rack after years of balancing damp aprons on whatever machinery was temporarily still. Each user has a marked section and must remove dry washing before adding more. The agreement nearly failed over the meaning of dry until a leather worker suggested touching the apron. A small collection paid for timber, with nails supplied by a resident who wished to see fewer of them borrowed. The rack has no keeper. Its users say they have enough people to remind one another when a sleeve is hanging in the wrong place.

times.headline: Stamp Album Exhibition Kept Behind Glass
times.body: A stationer has placed a customer's stamp album in the window for an afternoon exhibition. Visitors can compare the designs without handling the pages, and a list gives the owner's descriptions of the specimens. The display makes no promise about their value. Two prospective sellers have already asked to add figures to the list; both were referred to the owner. The stationer says the main result so far has been increased demand for clean paper and fewer fingerprints on his window. Children viewing the smallest stamps have been offered a stool, provided an adult holds it steady.

times.headline: Button Tin Helps Night Laundresses
times.body: A group of laundresses has established a common tin for buttons found in washing. Customers may look for a missing button when collecting clothes, but must describe it before emptying the contents onto the counter. The arrangement has recovered several sets that previously seemed beyond matching. One coat was reunited with a button its owner insisted had always been a different colour. No charge was made for the reunion. The laundresses ask that pins be removed before washing, since a button tin is useful while an unexpected pin is chiefly educational.

illustration.alt: Wet cobbles, a puddle, boots and an umbrella beside an old wooden door
illustration.caption: After the rain.

times.headline: Pie Queue Makes Room for a Porter
times.body: Customers waiting at a pie stall made room for a porter whose load prevented him from turning sideways. The stallholder passed his purchase over the queue, received payment by the same route and recovered the correct change after a brief accounting. A suggestion that all transactions be conducted this way was not adopted. The porter completed his delivery without setting the load in the street. One customer described the incident as ordinary courtesy; another said it had cost him his preferred pie. The stallholder has promised to make more of that sort tomorrow.

times.headline: Carver Restores a Weathered Sign
times.body: A sign carver has restored a shop board whose lettering had become illegible beneath several generations of paint. Removing the upper layers revealed the names of three earlier businesses. The present owner has kept a narrow strip of them visible at the edge, saying they explain several letters still arriving at his door. A former customer recognised the oldest name and supplied a sketch of its original border. The board now identifies the current shop clearly. It does not settle the customer’s outstanding claim for a chair, which predates both the present business and its proprietor.

times.headline: Stallholders Share an Awning
times.body: Three market stalls have agreed to share the cost of a new awning after discovering that each was paying to direct rain onto the next. The new canvas drains into a barrel belonging to the middle stallholder. He proposes to sell the water for washing vegetables, an arrangement his neighbours consider acceptable provided he does not first sell it back to them. The agreement includes a drawing of where each corner should be tied. This was added after the first fitting briefly turned the entire arrangement into a sail.

illustration.alt: A brass balance and iron weights beside baskets of onions and cabbages on a market counter
illustration.caption: Among the market stalls.

times.headline: Weights Returned with a Receipt
times.body: An elderly produce seller has recovered a box of weights borrowed during a busy market morning. The borrower returned them with a written list, prompting other traders to ask for copies of the form. The seller says the list matters less than remembering to bring things back. Her neighbour has nevertheless designed an elaborate receipt with space for two signatures. Its first use concerned a borrowed pencil. The pencil is still required to complete the second signature, so both parties have agreed to deal with that part verbally.

illustration.alt: A brass balance and iron weights beside baskets of onions and cabbages on a market counter
illustration.caption: Among the market stalls.

times.headline: Basket Scheme Eases the Market Round
times.body: A basket maker is lending sturdy carriers to customers who return them on the following market day. A small deposit covers damage, while repairs are charged according to the work required. The idea began when a customer dropped a week's vegetables through the bottom of an old basket. Several stallholders helped gather them before a passing cart arrived. The maker has reserved a shelf for returned carriers. He asks customers to remove their purchases first, especially when those purchases have begun expressing an opinion about being left there.

illustration.alt: A brass balance and iron weights beside baskets of onions and cabbages on a market counter
illustration.caption: Among the market stalls.

times.headline: Market Tally Gives Small Buyers a Turn
times.body: A produce stall has begun serving customers in the order marked on a slate rather than by the size of their baskets. The seller says the arrangement prevents a large order from repeatedly interrupting people buying one onion. A delivery assistant makes the marks and wipes them away after each sale. One customer attempted to purchase the slate itself to improve his position. The seller declined, observing that he would then need a new slate and the customer would still need an onion. The queue advanced without further innovation.

illustration.alt: A brass balance and iron weights beside baskets of onions and cabbages on a market counter
illustration.caption: Among the market stalls.

times.headline: Retired Baker Teaches the Late Batch
times.body: A retired baker has returned for two evenings each week to teach apprentices how to judge an oven without repeatedly opening it. The lessons include listening, waiting and resisting the urge to poke the bread. One apprentice reports that the last subject is the most demanding. The arrangement lets the working baker take a short rest before the morning batch. Payment consists of supper and a chair away from the draught. The retired baker has requested that the chair remain available even when his advice is not immediately followed.

illustration.alt: Loaves, a bread peel and flour beside an old brick bakehouse oven
illustration.caption: The early batch.

times.headline: Shared Oven Takes Numbered Trays
times.body: Neighbours using a small bakehouse oven have begun marking their trays with simple metal tokens. Several households had previously claimed whichever pie appeared least burnt. The baker now records each token beside its owner and returns the dish with its original expectations attached. Users still provide their own ingredients, and no judgement is made about the contents unless they escape onto another tray. A resident who cannot carry her dish is receiving help from two neighbours. They have asked for a token large enough to read without setting the supper down.

illustration.alt: Loaves, a bread peel and flour beside an old brick bakehouse oven
illustration.caption: The early batch.

times.headline: Loaves Set Aside for the Late Shift
times.body: A baker is holding back a small part of each day's bread for workers who cannot visit before the stalls close. Orders are taken in advance and kept under a clean cloth. The scheme follows requests from a laundress and two porters who often found only crumbs available after work. One customer has asked whether the arrangement could include warm bread. The baker says it can include bread, warmth being dependent on both the oven and the customer's punctuality. Those already using the scheme say the first promise is sufficient.

illustration.alt: Loaves, a bread peel and flour beside an old brick bakehouse oven
illustration.caption: The early batch.

times.headline: Bread Board Repaired Instead of Replaced
times.body: A bakehouse has repaired its longest serving bread board after an apprentice proposed throwing it away. A carpenter found that the damaged edge could be cut back and smoothed without losing the useful part. The cost was paid from money otherwise reserved for a new board. The apprentice has been asked to learn how the repair was made. He says this is a valuable lesson but would prefer the instruction to begin after the morning dough is finished. The carpenter agrees, having discovered that fresh dough is an exceptionally persistent way to mark one's tools.

illustration.alt: Loaves, a bread peel and flour beside an old brick bakehouse oven
illustration.caption: The early batch.

times.headline: Missing Tabby Returns to Two Homes
times.body: A grey tabby advertised as missing has been found dividing its time between two neighbouring households. Both owners correctly described the bell on its collar, and both supplied convincing accounts of feeding it. They have agreed to share the cost of a replacement collar and exchange notes about its meals. Neither wishes to give up the arrangement entirely. The cat attended the discussion from a wall and then left before the question of supper was settled. A fresh notice now asks neighbours to report illness or injury rather than every ordinary visit.

illustration.alt: A grey tabby with a collar bell sitting on a low courtyard wall
illustration.caption: A familiar courtyard visitor.

times.headline: Pet Notices Gain Clearer Descriptions
times.body: Readers placing missing-cat notices are being asked to include markings, collar details and a place for replies. Descriptions such as ordinary cat have proved less useful than hoped. One finder was visited by several owners who agreed only that the animal disliked being inspected. The newspaper's small-advertisement clerk suggests checking family drawings before commissioning a grander likeness. A child supplied the most useful sketch in a recent reunion. It included the cat's uneven ears and a careful warning that it did not enjoy being carried like a sack.

illustration.alt: A grey tabby with a collar bell sitting on a low courtyard wall
illustration.caption: A familiar courtyard visitor.

times.headline: Bell Maker Offers Quieter Fastenings
times.body: A maker of small collar bells is replacing loose fastenings after customers complained that their cats returned with the bell but without the collar. The revised fitting is demonstrated on a piece of leather rather than on an unwilling animal. Owners may bring an old collar to check its size. One customer asked for a bell loud enough to announce the cat from the next street. The maker has declined, explaining that a useful warning should not require the entire neighbourhood to participate in feeding time.

illustration.alt: A grey tabby with a collar bell sitting on a low courtyard wall
illustration.caption: A familiar courtyard visitor.

times.headline: Courtyard Keeps a Place for a Stray
times.body: Residents of a shared courtyard have set a covered box beside the washhouse for a stray tabby seen during cold nights. Each household has agreed to contribute a little food without leaving scraps across the passage. A child has painted the box, while a carpenter supplied a dry base raised above the paving. The residents make no claim that the cat will use it. It spent the first evening on top, apparently finding the arrangement satisfactory when viewed from another direction. The bedding remains available if it changes its mind.

illustration.alt: A grey tabby with a collar bell sitting on a low courtyard wall
illustration.caption: A familiar courtyard visitor.

times.headline: Rain Barrel Agreement Protects the Passage
times.body: Two households have moved a rain barrel after complaints that its overflow made their shared passage slippery. The new position feeds a small channel beside the wall. A neighbour supplied a flat stone to bridge the channel, allowing baskets and boots to cross without entering the water. Discussion of who should pay ended when everyone counted the materials they already possessed. The work took less time than the preceding correspondence. Residents ask that the barrel remain for collecting rain rather than become convenient storage for things nobody wishes to carry upstairs.

illustration.alt: Wet cobbles, a puddle, boots and an umbrella beside an old wooden door
illustration.caption: After the rain.

times.headline: Doorstep Mat Trial Reduces Mud
times.body: A boarding house has placed a stout mat inside its street door and supplied a brush for boot soles. The keeper reports less mud on the stair and more argument at the entrance about whose turn it is to use the brush. An additional brush has therefore been ordered. Lodgers remain responsible for their own boots; the keeper specifically excludes mysterious changes in colour after cleaning. A porter says he had forgotten what colour his boots were and considers the discovery an unexpected benefit of paying attention to the notice.

illustration.alt: Wet cobbles, a puddle, boots and an umbrella beside an old wooden door
illustration.caption: After the rain.

times.headline: Paving Crew Records a Reusable Repair
times.body: A small paving crew has begun keeping drawings of repaired patches so the stones can be lifted and replaced without repeating the whole arrangement. The notes distinguish drains, doorstep edges and the places where carts are most likely to turn. One householder welcomed the drawings until he discovered that his favourite loose stone had been described as loose. The crew says it can be made firm without altering its appearance. He has agreed, provided they return it to the same corner. Work will proceed when the neighbouring delivery is complete.

illustration.alt: Wet cobbles, a puddle, boots and an umbrella beside an old wooden door
illustration.caption: After the rain.

times.headline: Umbrella Rack Returns a Doorway to Use
times.body: A shopkeeper has installed a narrow rack for wet umbrellas after customers began leaving them open across the entrance. The rack holds them closed over a shallow tray. Its maker has asked customers not to test it by leaning on it, an instruction added after an unexpectedly enthusiastic demonstration. The shopkeeper says the doorway is now usable and the floor easier to dry. A regular customer has suggested reserving a place for walking sticks. This will be considered once everyone stops claiming the same perfectly ordinary black umbrella.

illustration.alt: Wet cobbles, a puddle, boots and an umbrella beside an old wooden door
illustration.caption: After the rain.

inquirer.headline: HAT SWALLOWS WIZARD'S AFTERNOON
inquirer.body: An unnamed wizard says he reached into his hat for a handkerchief and lost track of the afternoon. Onlookers say he was asleep. Our correspondent cannot rule out a temporal disturbance, particularly one occurring after lunch. The hat has refused an interview and continues to look unusually well rested.

illustration.alt: A wizard hat, biscuits, teapot and a simple seating plan on an old stone-room table
illustration.caption: From the University desk.

inquirer.headline: SAUSAGE SURVIVES FALL FROM CART
inquirer.body: A sausage has survived a fall onto the cobbles with what witnesses describe as an alarming bounce. The vendor calls this proof of quality. A customer asks which quality. The sausage was last seen rolling towards a drain, apparently seeking a less demanding market.

inquirer.headline: MYSTERY FOOTPRINTS FOLLOW BOOTS
inquirer.body: Residents awoke to a trail of mysterious prints following a delivery man's boots through fresh mud. The man says this is normal. But why those boots? Why that mud? And why was our reporter required to move aside? Questions remain, mostly because everyone else has gone to work.

inquirer.headline: DOOR KNOCKER STRIKES AGAIN
inquirer.body: A resident claims his door knocker has disturbed him repeatedly over several days. Visitors have been observed near the scene. Experts suggest a connection, but the householder demands stronger action. He has now removed the knocker, leaving callers to strike the door in a far less civilised manner.

inquirer.headline: BARGAIN MIRROR KNOWS YOUR FACE
inquirer.body: A second-hand mirror is said to recognise every customer placed before it. Its seller denies sorcery and points to the price. One nervous buyer says the image moved when he did. We advise readers to approach with caution, especially if they have recently had an unfortunate haircut.

inquirer.headline: RIVER REFUSES TO EXPLAIN ITSELF
inquirer.body: The river continued flowing yesterday despite repeated attempts to establish where all of it was going. A boatman offered an explanation involving the sea. That merely raises further questions. Our reporter is pursuing the matter from the bank, where the investigation is considerably less damp.

illustration.alt: A cargo barge tied to a timber bollard with thick mooring ropes beside old river warehouses
illustration.caption: At the river wharves.

inquirer.headline: WOMAN FINDS OTHER GLOVE
inquirer.body: A local woman has found the glove missing since last winter inside her other glove. Neighbours are calling for an inquiry into how long it had been there. The woman has asked them to leave. Our readers deserve answers, though preferably without having to search their own pockets.

inquirer.headline: GUILD MEETING ENDS WITHOUT FEAST
inquirer.body: Shock swept a meeting when members discovered the refreshments were scheduled for next week. Delegates debated whether business could continue under such conditions. A biscuit was divided into portions too small to restore confidence. Organisers promise lessons have been learned and have ordered a larger biscuit.

inquirer.headline: BENCH REMEMBERS EVERY BOTTOM
inquirer.body: A carpenter claims marks on a public bench record years of civic life. Could wood be watching us? He says no, mostly it is buckles. This paper will continue asking the difficult questions until someone explains why the bench was positioned directly opposite our office.

inquirer.headline: MAN CLAIMS TO OWN TOMORROW'S RAIN
inquirer.body: An enterprising citizen is offering reservations on tomorrow's rain. Customers receive a bucket and instructions to wait. He says this is an investment in natural resources. Complaints will be accepted when the weather improves, a condition which has greatly reduced pressure on his customer service department.

inquirer.headline: TWO SOUPS, ONE LADLE: CATERING SCANDAL
inquirer.body: Diners are demanding answers after discovering two soups shared a ladle. The cook says they were served on different days. Is that what they want us to think? A third soup could not be reached for comment, having already been declared yesterday's special.

inquirer.headline: INVISIBLE CAT BLAMED FOR EMPTY DISH
inquirer.body: A resident claims an invisible cat is visiting nightly and consuming milk. Her visible cat appeared reluctant to assist our inquiry. The dish is certainly empty. We cannot dismiss the possibility of a second cat, particularly while the first is licking its whiskers behind our notebook.

inquirer.headline: POTATO LOOKS LIKE MAN WHO OWES MONEY
inquirer.body: A gardener has produced a potato resembling a man who owes his neighbour money. The neighbour says the resemblance is exact around the eyes. The gardener denies cultivating debtors deliberately. We publish no name, pending identification and confirmation that the potato has sufficient funds.

inquirer.headline: CLOCK STEALS TWELVE MINUTES
inquirer.body: Workers blame a slow clock for twelve missing minutes. The owner promises to put them back on the next winding. But where have those minutes been? A nearby clerk believes they were used for tea. We shall investigate after our own entirely necessary refreshment break.

inquirer.headline: WIZARD'S LAUNDRY DEFIES EXPECTATIONS
inquirer.body: A robe returned from washing smaller than its owner remembers. The washerwoman points to a label advising against everything she was asked to do. Is the robe shrinking, or is the wizard growing? Our measuring tape was confiscated before a satisfactory answer could be obtained.

inquirer.headline: MISSING LADDER FOUND ABOVE GROUND
inquirer.body: A ladder reported missing has been found leaning against a wall. Its owner says he looked everywhere except upwards. Residents fear other objects may be hiding in plain sight. We urge readers to inspect their surroundings before purchasing our forthcoming guide to inspecting their surroundings.

inquirer.headline: SHOP WINDOW REVEALS EVERYTHING INSIDE
inquirer.body: A merchant has installed a transparent pane allowing passers-by to see goods without entering. Rivals call the practice intrusive. Customers say it is useful when the shop is shut. Our exclusive investigation reveals the view is considerably less impressive when somebody stands in front of it.

inquirer.headline: BARREL MAKES BID FOR FREEDOM
inquirer.body: A barrel escaped its cart on a slope yesterday and travelled further than several paying passengers. The cooper denies designing it for speed. Witnesses describe a round suspect moving downhill. Anyone offering it shelter should be aware it contains pickled onions and has no known brakes.

inquirer.headline: LANTERN CASTS SUSPICIOUS SHADOW
inquirer.body: A resident reports a shadow moving whenever he carries his lantern. Could someone be following him? A neighbour says yes, his shadow. This explanation has failed to satisfy the resident, who objects that nobody asked permission. Further sightings are expected immediately after dark.

inquirer.headline: THE GREAT TURNIP COVER-UP
inquirer.body: A competition turnip arrived beneath a cloth, provoking fevered speculation about its appearance. Judges say the cloth was simply keeping off flies. Why were the flies interested? What do they know? We have requested an interview with the grower, preferably before the turnip is made into supper.

inquirer.headline: NEW BROOM HAS HIDDEN PAST
inquirer.body: A buyer has discovered his new broom was previously used to demonstrate sweeping. The merchant insists it remains substantially new. How many floors did it see? What corners were overlooked? The purchaser demands the truth and a partial refund, though he would settle for the refund.

inquirer.headline: QUEUE FORMS WITHOUT EXPLANATION
inquirer.body: A queue formed outside a closed shop after one man stopped to tie his boot. Others assumed he knew something. He now fears leaving will cause disappointment. This paper supports the public's right to know what it is waiting for, once our reporter reaches the front.

inquirer.headline: MYSTERY NOISE EXPOSED AS OTHER NOISE
inquirer.body: A mysterious midnight rattling has been traced to a loose shutter, raising urgent questions about why the shutter was loose. The owner blames wind. We have been unable to obtain a statement from the wind, which passed our reporter without stopping despite a clearly spoken request.

inquirer.headline: MAN TAKES UMBRELLA TO BED
inquirer.body: A resident sleeping beneath a leaking roof has taken an umbrella to bed. His landlord praises the tenant's resourcefulness. The tenant requests tiles. Can a man be too prepared? Readers with similar experiences should write in, taking care to keep their letters above the waterline.

illustration.alt: Wet cobbles, a puddle, boots and an umbrella beside an old wooden door
illustration.caption: After the rain.

inquirer.headline: WIZARD'S BISCUIT MAP SHOCK
inquirer.body: A flour-dusted scrap said to reveal a secret plan at Unseen University has turned out to be a seating arrangement for refreshments. That has not discouraged the man who found it. He maintains that the circles plainly show positions of power. A baker who examined the paper says they show where the plates went. The finder is considering a lecture, admission by arrangement, while the baker has offered to demonstrate his theory with actual biscuits. Our correspondent favours further investigation of the baker's evidence. No University official has endorsed either explanation or purchased a ticket.

illustration.alt: A wizard hat, biscuits, teapot and a simple seating plan on an old stone-room table
illustration.caption: From the University desk.

inquirer.headline: MESSAGE IN BOTTLE FAILS TO LEAVE ANKH
inquirer.body: A man attempting to send a message by river has recovered the same bottle below his own window. He says it must have made a complete journey and returned with unusual speed. His neighbour says it struck a sack and stayed there. The message, which asks whether anybody is listening, remains unanswered. A second attempt will use a larger bottle, a proposal warmly supported by the bottle seller. Readers claiming to have received the first message should explain how they read it without disturbing the cork, which still bears the sender's teeth marks.

illustration.alt: A cargo barge tied to a timber bollard with thick mooring ropes beside old river warehouses
illustration.caption: At the river wharves.

inquirer.headline: BOOTS BRING STREET INTO BEDROOM
inquirer.body: A resident who found a mysterious line of grit from his door to his bed initially blamed an intruder. Examination of his boots has supplied an alternative suspect. He accepts that they carried a quantity of the road indoors, but disputes responsibility for the arrangement of the stones. His landlady has suggested a mat. He fears this would interfere with any further investigation. The Inquirer can report that no supernatural activity has been established and that the floor still requires sweeping. The landlady regards the second finding as the more urgent.

illustration.alt: Wet cobbles, a puddle, boots and an umbrella beside an old wooden door
illustration.caption: After the rain.

inquirer.headline: OPERA GHOST DEMANDS SECOND TICKET
inquirer.body: A theatre enthusiast has demanded a refund after the empty seat beside him was sold to another customer. He says he had reserved it for the ghost he hoped would attend. The clerk says the second customer both paid and appeared, two qualities the proposed ghost did not demonstrate. A dispute over the word reserved has followed. Neither customer wishes to miss the performance, and the seat is now occupied by a coat. Its owner has been asked to remove it. The ghost, if present, has so far preferred the cheaper accommodation of being unobserved.

illustration.alt: Carpenter tools, ropes and timber braces behind a painted palace set in an opera house
illustration.caption: Behind the scenery.

inquirer.headline: SLIPPERS TOO FIERCE FOR THE PARLOUR
inquirer.body: A shop displaying metal-reinforced slippers has withdrawn its claim that they are suitable for every home after a buyer returned with an injured table leg. The maker says the slippers performed precisely as designed. The buyer says his family expected quieter evenings. A dwarf metalworker consulted by this paper admired the hinges but questioned the need for them. The shop now describes the product as specialist indoor footwear and offers felt pads separately. No customer has yet returned a pair because they wore out, although two have asked how to stop them announcing arrivals.

inquirer.headline: TROLL'S EAR MUFFS BAFFLE HAT SELLER
inquirer.body: A hat seller has discovered that the two small cushions ordered by a troll customer were intended to reduce the noise of a neighbour's hammering, rather than keep out the cold. He had been advertising them for the wrong purpose. The customer says the misunderstanding matters less than whether they work. Trials were interrupted when the neighbour came round to ask why nobody had answered his knock. The seller has removed his weather claims and offered sturdier ties. The hammering continues, but at least one household now knows when to expect it.

inquirer.headline: LOVE MESSAGE ARRIVES WITH BARREL ORDER
inquirer.body: A clerk who copied a private note onto the back of a clacks order has apologised after the recipient received both a demand for barrels and a declaration of affection. The recipient describes the combination as businesslike. The clerk's intended correspondent has asked whether the barrels were also meant for them. No engagement has been announced, and the barrels remain a separate transaction. Our advice columnist believes a second note is needed. Our commercial correspondent recommends checking which side of the paper it is written on before paying for transmission.

illustration.alt: Clerks with dispatch forms and quills beside a clacks tower with square shutter panels
illustration.caption: Messages across the city.

inquirer.headline: MIRROR REFUSES DISCOUNT
inquirer.body: A barber's notice promising younger looks has prompted a customer to demand a reduction after the shop mirror offered no support for the claim. The barber says the improvement lies in presentation. The customer has offered to present less money. A neighbouring stallholder proposed turning the mirror to the wall until agreement could be reached. This was rejected because it made shaving difficult. The notice has now been amended to promise a haircut. Both parties agree that a haircut occurred, although they remain divided over how successfully the hair participated.

inquirer.headline: DRUM CHAIR RETIRES UNBEATEN
inquirer.body: A chair removed from the Mended Drum has been declared beyond repair by a carpenter who says it contains too many earlier repairs to identify the original problem. An interested buyer calls this evidence of exceptional durability. The carpenter calls it mostly nails. The chair is being offered as material rather than furniture, with no guarantee that it will remain a single item during collection. A second buyer has asked whether it comes with its reputation. The seller is prepared to discuss this, provided the buyer does not attempt to sit down while negotiations are continuing.

inquirer.headline: VOLUNTEER FINDS GOD ALREADY REPRESENTED
inquirer.body: A man offering to organise a new religious collection discovered that the deity named on his box already had several worshippers present. They asked where the money would go. He replied that arrangements were still developing. The box was consequently converted into a collection for repairing its owner's handcart, an enterprise everyone could inspect. Contributions were modest but sufficient for a wheel pin. The owner says he has learnt the value of clarity. His first clear act was to paint over the word temple before taking the cart away.

inquirer.headline: DOG PORTRAIT REJECTED BY DOG
inquirer.body: A merchant who commissioned a portrait of his dog says the animal has refused to acknowledge it. The artist points out that dogs are not dependable judges of likeness. The merchant replies that this one is otherwise very observant. Attempts to improve the sitting ended when the dog took possession of the painter's lunch. The portrait will remain as it is, with a small adjustment to the account for the missing food. No artistic movement is claimed. The dog has expressed continued interest in another sitting if the same provisions can be arranged.

inquirer.headline: RED ROBE STARTS LAUNDRY FEUD
inquirer.body: A wash intended to brighten several white shirts has instead produced a row of pale pink ones. A red robe is assisting enquiries by being conspicuously red. Its owner disputes the suggestion that he should pay for every shirt, arguing that the effect is evenly distributed and therefore fair. The laundress says fairness was not on the washing instructions. A compromise involving separate tubs is being considered. Meanwhile, a stallholder has offered to buy the shirts as a matching set, provided nobody describes their colour to his customers as an accident.

inquirer.headline: STAR WATCHER DISCOVERS ROOFTOP
inquirer.body: An amateur observer who reported a new and unusually square body in the night sky has identified it as a neighbour's chimney. The discovery followed a change in the position of his viewing tube. He says the error demonstrates the importance of keeping careful records. His neighbour says it demonstrates the importance of looking up. The observer intends to publish both explanations together and has withdrawn his proposed name for the object. It remains available, he says, for the next genuine discovery. The neighbour would prefer the chimney not to be discovered again.

inquirer.headline: SAUSAGE PUTS SCALES UNDER STRAIN
inquirer.body: An argument at a street-food stall concerns whether a sausage should be priced by length, weight or the purchaser's confidence. The seller favours whichever method produces the least argument before lunch. A customer brought scales, but their pan proved too small and the demonstration required a plate borrowed from another stall. The plate's owner then requested payment for its use. All parties are considering a single combined price, though none agrees what it should include. This paper can confirm the sausage existed at the start of the discussion. Its subsequent whereabouts are disputed.

inquirer.headline: HAT CLAIMS DISTINGUISHED ANCESTORS
inquirer.body: A second-hand hat has been offered at an increased price after its seller discovered an old name written inside the band. He cannot establish which person of that name owned it, but believes the uncertainty should increase interest. A customer suggested it might be the hat maker. The seller says this would still give it a respectable trade background. A second name has since been found beneath the first. Anyone claiming the hat should bring a description, rather than a family tree. The seller currently charges extra for the family tree.

inquirer.headline: FORTUNE TELLER DEMANDS BETTER CALENDAR
inquirer.body: A fortune teller who advertised an excellent day for journeys has explained that the prediction referred to a different day. Rain had discouraged most of the proposed journeys before the correction appeared. Customers offered replacement fortunes may ask to retain the originals for comparison. The fortune teller considers this an unfair approach to future events. A nearby calendar seller has offered to assist with the past ones. No partnership has been agreed. The Inquirer will report developments as they occur, which our printing department assures us is the usual order in which reports should be produced.

inquirer.headline: ONION BLAMED FOR COLLAPSE IN TESTIMONY
inquirer.body: A market argument about short weight ended with several people in tears after a seller cut open an onion to demonstrate the quality of his stock. One witness says this proves the vegetables are dangerous. The seller says it proves the onion was fresh. Our reporter requested a second demonstration and has since submitted an unusually brief account. The scales have not been accused of crying, although they remain central to the original disagreement. Customers are advised that a powerful emotional experience is not automatically included in the price of every purchase.

illustration.alt: A brass balance and iron weights beside baskets of onions and cabbages on a market counter
illustration.caption: Among the market stalls.

inquirer.headline: CABBAGE PRICE CAUSES SECOND LOOK
inquirer.body: A customer who misread a cabbage price as the cost of the whole stall attempted to take possession of the counter, awning and scales. The seller says the figure applied to one cabbage. The customer disputes whether anything so small can justify such a large-looking number. A clearer sign has been ordered. The cabbage remains unsold, giving both parties time to consider their next offer. A neighbour has proposed buying it jointly and cutting it in half, an apparently simple plan that now requires agreement about who receives the stalk.

illustration.alt: A brass balance and iron weights beside baskets of onions and cabbages on a market counter
illustration.caption: Among the market stalls.

inquirer.headline: SCALES WEIGH THEIR OWN REPUTATION
inquirer.body: A trader demonstrating his new balance placed an old set of weights in one pan and the new weights in the other. The result has encouraged vigorous discussion and no immediate confidence. He says the discrepancy may lie in the counter. The counter's owner objects to this suggestion. A third trader has offered to weigh the counter, provided somebody first removes it from the stall. The Inquirer is following developments at a prudent distance from the lifting. There is no confirmed evidence that a thumb was involved, although several have been pointed.

illustration.alt: A brass balance and iron weights beside baskets of onions and cabbages on a market counter
illustration.caption: Among the market stalls.

inquirer.headline: MARKET AWNING TAKES SIDES
inquirer.body: An awning that sheltered two stalls successfully has directed most of its accumulated rain onto a third. The affected trader suspects a deliberate adjustment. His neighbours blame the position of the rope, which is less expensive to accuse. A new knot has been tied under supervision. The next shower will determine whether this constitutes a settlement or merely an adjournment. Meanwhile, customers may identify the disputed stall by its unusually clean cabbages. The proprietor has rejected suggestions that he advertise this as a complimentary washing service until his boots have dried.

illustration.alt: A brass balance and iron weights beside baskets of onions and cabbages on a market counter
illustration.caption: Among the market stalls.

inquirer.headline: BAKER DENIES SELLING THE HOLES
inquirer.body: A baker accused of charging for an unusually airy loaf says customers are purchasing the bread around the spaces. An angry buyer maintains that the spaces occupy the best part of the purchase. The baker has offered a heavier loaf, which the buyer describes as a different complaint waiting to happen. A practical neighbour resolved the immediate dispute by making toast. Both parties accepted a slice and postponed the discussion until breakfast was over. The Inquirer cannot establish whether the original loaf was exceptional, since its surviving evidence now consists chiefly of crumbs.

illustration.alt: Loaves, a bread peel and flour beside an old brick bakehouse oven
illustration.caption: The early batch.

inquirer.headline: OVEN WARMER THAN ADVERTISED ROOM
inquirer.body: A lodger has asked why the baker next door enjoys better heating than the room he rents. His landlord says the distinction lies in the room's intended use. The lodger proposes making bread in it. This suggestion has not been welcomed, especially after he requested permission to widen the chimney. The baker has offered him a warm seat while the first batch cools, provided he does not fall asleep against the flour sacks. Negotiations continue over whether a loaf purchased during the visit should count towards rent or breakfast.

illustration.alt: Loaves, a bread peel and flour beside an old brick bakehouse oven
illustration.caption: The early batch.

inquirer.headline: BREAD PEEL PROPOSED FOR ACADEMIC HONOUR
inquirer.body: A baker's assistant claims the shop's wooden peel deserves recognition for completing years of dependable work without once requesting a day off. The baker says it has received regular oiling and should be content. A customer has suggested an honorary handle, prompting objections from people who believe it already has one. No University has been approached. The assistant says this is because he wishes to keep the award dignified. The peel continues to work as usual, which our correspondent regards as the strongest available argument in its favour.

illustration.alt: Loaves, a bread peel and flour beside an old brick bakehouse oven
illustration.caption: The early batch.

inquirer.headline: APPRENTICE DISCOVERS CRUST WAS OUTSIDE
inquirer.body: A new bakehouse apprentice asked to improve the crust removed it from a sample loaf and presented it separately for inspection. The baker has clarified that future improvements should remain attached to the bread. The apprentice says the instruction was incomplete. A written list of duties is being prepared, with additional space for interpretations nobody has yet anticipated. Customers who purchased the separated pieces report no difficulty making use of them. One asked whether the arrangement could be repeated at a lower price, a question that has caused the baker to reconsider his objection.

illustration.alt: Loaves, a bread peel and flour beside an old brick bakehouse oven
illustration.caption: The early batch.

inquirer.headline: TABBY ACCUSED OF RUNNING DINNER RING
inquirer.body: A grey tabby with a collar bell is suspected of obtaining supper from several households by appearing hungry at each door. Residents comparing notes found that the animal's schedule was better organised than their own. A proposed meeting to settle feeding arrangements was interrupted when the cat arrived and looked hungry. No agreement was reached. One householder insists the cat has an honest face. Another points out that this may be essential to its method. The Inquirer reminds readers that feline expressions are not a substitute for comparing how many meals have already been served.

illustration.alt: A grey tabby with a collar bell sitting on a low courtyard wall
illustration.caption: A familiar courtyard visitor.

inquirer.headline: CAT KNOWS WHICH HOUSE HAS FISH
inquirer.body: A tabby has repeatedly visited the only courtyard household cooking fish, leading its owner to suggest an extraordinary gift of prediction. Neighbours favour an explanation involving smell. The owner considers this insufficiently impressive and has offered a demonstration when fish is next available. The cat has accepted no formal engagement but is expected to attend. Our reporter will observe from the doorway and has declined the proposed fee. Readers should note that no school of wizardry has confirmed the claim, and the cat has not supplied its qualifications in writing.

illustration.alt: A grey tabby with a collar bell sitting on a low courtyard wall
illustration.caption: A familiar courtyard visitor.

inquirer.headline: COLLAR BELL BREAKS SILENCE SCANDAL
inquirer.body: A cat owner who fitted a quieter bell says his household can no longer tell where the animal has gone. The cat appears satisfied with the improvement. The bell maker says quieter was the agreed specification and offers a louder replacement at the ordinary price. A neighbour has proposed keeping the present bell and looking out of the window. This has been described as an unnecessarily manual approach. Talks resumed after the cat returned and rang the bell by scratching behind its ear, demonstrating that it was perfectly capable of making an announcement when it chose.

illustration.alt: A grey tabby with a collar bell sitting on a low courtyard wall
illustration.caption: A familiar courtyard visitor.

inquirer.headline: COURTYARD WALL UNDER FELINE MANAGEMENT
inquirer.body: Residents who usually leave baskets on a low courtyard wall have discovered that a tabby now occupies the warmest section. Attempts to move the baskets nearer have been met with a look described by witnesses as administrative. The wall's owner says no formal tenancy exists. Other residents ask whether this means anyone is free to sit there, a question he would prefer not to answer. The cat remains in possession. An offered cushion was accepted briefly before being occupied sideways, leaving most of the animal on the original stone.

illustration.alt: A grey tabby with a collar bell sitting on a low courtyard wall
illustration.caption: A familiar courtyard visitor.

inquirer.headline: PUDDLE CLAIMS THIRD BOOT
inquirer.body: A deep-looking puddle has been blamed for wetting three boots outside the same doorway. Examination suggests that the fourth boot belonged to a man who stepped around it. He has been asked to demonstrate his method for the benefit of local residents. The demonstration is free, although a nearby vendor is offering a written account for those unable to attend. Our correspondent has inspected the route and confirms that it involves moving slightly to one side. Authorities on the subject warn that success still depends on noticing the puddle before entering it.

illustration.alt: Wet cobbles, a puddle, boots and an umbrella beside an old wooden door
illustration.caption: After the rain.

inquirer.headline: UMBRELLA REFUSES TO SHARE CREDIT
inquirer.body: A man who congratulated himself on arriving home dry discovered that he had left his borrowed umbrella at the door of the person he was visiting. The owner says the umbrella deserves more recognition for the journey. The borrower has offered thanks and a replacement strap, but objects to giving it an individual mention in this newspaper. We have nevertheless done so in the public interest. Further borrowing is suspended until the strap is fitted. The weather remains free to complicate the matter, and has already supplied several suggestions.

illustration.alt: Wet cobbles, a puddle, boots and an umbrella beside an old wooden door
illustration.caption: After the rain.

inquirer.headline: BOOTS FOUND HIDING UNDER MUD
inquirer.body: A pair of boots cleaned after a wet patrol through the streets has turned out to be considerably smaller than its owner remembered. He says the mud provided useful support and objects to paying for its removal. The cleaner says the original request was quite specific. They have agreed to try thicker socks before discussing any further remedy. No evidence of shrinking leather has been established. The owner has declined an offer to return the mud in a separate bag, explaining that the cleaner has failed to preserve the shape in which it was working best.

illustration.alt: Wet cobbles, a puddle, boots and an umbrella beside an old wooden door
illustration.caption: After the rain.

inquirer.headline: DOORWAY WEATHER OBSERVER STAYS DRY
inquirer.body: An amateur weather observer has completed a week of reports without leaving his doorstep, an achievement he regards as evidence of practical judgement. Critics say his accounts reveal little about conditions beyond the door. He replies that everyone beyond it appears wet. A proposed expedition to the other side of the street was postponed after a cart passed through a puddle. The observer is now gathering information from umbrellas left nearby. Their usefulness as instruments remains unproven, although they have successfully informed him that several neighbours would like them back.

illustration.alt: Wet cobbles, a puddle, boots and an umbrella beside an old wooden door
illustration.caption: After the rain.

classifieds.headline: Lost: brass watch
classifieds.body: Plain brass watch, dent on lid. Reward for return upon identification. Please check your own waistcoat before applying.

classifieds.headline: Found: single boot
classifieds.body: Right boot found beside a left turn. Owner should describe contents, if any. We have not investigated closely.

classifieds.headline: Missing: soup ladle
classifieds.body: Large ladle missing after neighbourhood supper. Return welcomed. Explanation optional; soup already cold.

classifieds.headline: Lost: green scarf
classifieds.body: Long green scarf, one end longer than the other. Modest reward. Please do not bring snakes on speculation.

classifieds.headline: Found: bunch of keys
classifieds.body: Seven keys and something believed to open a tin. Owner may demonstrate ownership using a door that belongs to them.

classifieds.headline: Missing: delivery sack
classifieds.body: Empty sack last seen carrying an entirely different empty sack. Neither answers to a name. Return either for thanks.

classifieds.headline: Lost: spectacles
classifieds.body: Round spectacles in brown case. Owner unable to give useful directions until they are found. Ask for the squinting gentleman.

classifieds.headline: Found: walking stick
classifieds.body: Stout stick, silver-coloured handle. Owner should identify the initials. Anyone claiming 'all of them' will be turned away.

classifieds.headline: Missing: red umbrella
classifieds.body: Red umbrella taken in error during rain. Replacement umbrella left behind is mostly holes. Exchange requested when convenient, preferably before rain.

classifieds.headline: Lost: account book
classifieds.body: Small account book. Reward exceeds its apparent value. Finder requested not to improve the figures.

classifieds.headline: Found: false tooth
classifieds.body: Single tooth found in an apple. Both await identification. Only the tooth need be collected.

classifieds.headline: Lost: pair of gloves
classifieds.body: Brown gloves. Possibly together, possibly pursuing separate interests. Reward for either; better reward for both.

classifieds.headline: Missing: kettle lid
classifieds.body: Lid only. Kettle remains at home and has become impossible to ignore. Please return before breakfast.

classifieds.headline: Found: parcel string
classifieds.body: Excellent length of string. Owner should describe knot. No reward sought; we simply dislike waste.

classifieds.headline: Lost: wooden duck
classifieds.body: Child's wooden duck on wheels. Much missed. Reward and relieved household for safe return. Real ducks will not be accepted.

classifieds.headline: Missing: tool bag
classifieds.body: Canvas bag containing hammer, pliers and an unreasonable number of bent nails. Honest return preferred to creative explanations.

classifieds.headline: Found: purse, empty
classifieds.body: Purse found empty. Owner may collect purse. Contents remain a separate and considerably more interesting matter.

classifieds.headline: Lost: hat
classifieds.body: Black hat with narrow brim. Not the black hat with wide brim currently offered to everyone. Owner knows the difference.

classifieds.headline: Room to let
classifieds.body: Small upper room. Fine view if tenant supplies ladder. No practising spells, breeding livestock or moving internal walls.

classifieds.headline: Wanted: honest porter
classifieds.body: Steady porter wanted. Must distinguish 'fragile' from 'please demonstrate strength'. References should concern carrying things.

classifieds.headline: Second-hand chair
classifieds.body: Chair for sale. Three reliable legs; fourth offers opportunities. Buyer collects and should avoid sudden celebrations.

classifieds.headline: Mended pots
classifieds.body: Pots repaired while you wait, or later if you prefer not to watch. Previous repairs discussed discreetly.

classifieds.headline: Wanted: proofreader
classifieds.body: Proofreader wanted. Applicants should find the error in this notice. Employer reserves the right to add one later.

classifieds.headline: Barrels available
classifieds.body: Empty barrels, several sizes. Previous contents known in most cases. Buyer advised against testing by smell alone.

classifieds.headline: Boots resoled
classifieds.body: Good soles fitted to existing boots. We cannot repair the decisions which brought you here, but can improve the walk home.

classifieds.headline: Laundry taken in
classifieds.body: Laundry accepted by weight. Stones in pockets charged separately. Unexplained stains need no accompanying story.

classifieds.headline: Quiet lodger wanted
classifieds.body: Quiet lodger sought. Existing lodger is quiet but plays trombone. Applicants must understand the distinction.

classifieds.headline: Sausages: exceptional value
classifieds.body: A Dibbler enterprise. Hot sausages available while temperature permits. Purchasers encouraged to bring their own optimism.

classifieds.headline: Notice copying
classifieds.body: Clear notices copied in a legible hand. We reproduce spelling as supplied unless paid to argue.

classifieds.headline: Wanted: missing sign
classifieds.body: Shopkeeper seeks sign reading OPEN. Until returned, business continues despite contrary appearances.

classifieds.headline: Cabbages delivered
classifieds.body: Cabbages delivered to your door. Admission not required. Please leave sufficient room for disappointment if you ordered something else.

classifieds.headline: Repairs undertaken
classifieds.body: Small household repairs. Estimates free; agreement with estimates not guaranteed. No bridges, towers or things which have begun speaking.

classifieds.headline: Lost: silver watch and chain
classifieds.body: Family watch, scratched crescent inside lid; reward upon correct identification. Time shown unreliable. Sentimental value considerable; please do not send estimates of the scrap value. Reply Box 201.

classifieds.headline: Missing: elderly tabby
classifieds.body: Grey tabby, torn left ear, usually unimpressed by visitors. Please report sightings rather than feed him a second breakfast. Reward for safe return. Reply Box 202.

classifieds.headline: Found: parcel of knitting
classifieds.body: Three unfinished socks and a note expressing disappointment. Owner should identify colour and explain the third sock. No charge for return. Reply Box 203.

classifieds.headline: Room to let: quiet tenant sought
classifieds.body: Small upper room, shared stair and washstand. A person who works nights is welcome if they come home quietly. View by arrangement; do not simply climb the drainpipe. Reply Box 204.

classifieds.headline: Lost: dwarf's leather apron
classifieds.body: Dark leather, repaired buckle, pocket containing a folded shopping list. Reward offered for the apron. Owner is particularly anxious to recover the list before going shopping again. Reply Box 205.

classifieds.headline: Found: brass collar bell
classifieds.body: No animal attached. Please describe the fastening before claiming. Finder would also appreciate learning how it got into a closed flour tin. Reply Box 206.

classifieds.headline: Second-hand pram
classifieds.body: Sound wheels, good hood, occupant not included. One wheel squeaks on corners; price allows for the buyer's opinion on this. Inspection welcome. Reply Box 207.

classifieds.headline: Wanted: patient copyist
classifieds.body: Clear handwriting required for a family account book. Must copy figures as supplied, rather than improving them. References and a short sample requested. Reply Box 208.

classifieds.headline: Lost: spectacles in brown case
classifieds.body: Likely left at a market counter. Reward for return; finder should not judge the prescription without first taking them off. Large-print replies appreciated. Box 209.

classifieds.headline: Missing: green parrot
classifieds.body: Answers to several names, most unsuitable for this notice. Reward for return unharmed. Statements made by bird are not admissions by owner. Reply Box 210.

classifieds.headline: For sale: carpenter's bench
classifieds.body: Heavy bench, two useful vices and several less useful opinions carved underneath. Buyer collects with help. Legs included; assistance carrying it is not. Reply Box 211.

classifieds.headline: Wanted: a reliable lodger
classifieds.body: Evening use of kitchen available. No disputes about who owns yesterday's gravy. Rent and household arrangements agreed before moving in. Reply Box 212.

classifieds.headline: Lost: child's wooden horse
classifieds.body: Small carved toy, blue saddle, one repaired ear. Modest reward offered by a family who would very much like it back. Reply Box 213.

classifieds.headline: Found: key tied to red ribbon
classifieds.body: Large iron key recovered from a basket. Owner should describe the ribbon and provide a convincing reason not to try it in every door. Reply Box 214.

classifieds.headline: Sewing repairs undertaken
classifieds.body: Hems, cuffs, pockets and honest patches. Garments returned clean if delivered clean. Please empty pockets; unusual contents do not reduce the bill. Reply Box 215.

classifieds.headline: Companion sought for early walks
classifieds.body: Retired porter seeks steady company for short morning walks. No wagers on distance and no obligation to discuss knees. Reply Box 216.

classifieds.headline: Lost: wedding ring
classifieds.body: Plain band; initials inside available to verify ownership. Reward. Please reply privately; the entire household has already offered advice about the matter. Box 217.

classifieds.headline: Missing: tortoise
classifieds.body: Small, brown, determined. Last observed leaving the garden at a pace not immediately recognised as escape. Reward for a useful sighting. No racing proposals. Reply Box 218.

classifieds.headline: For sale: two matched chairs
classifieds.body: Matched to each other, not to any known table. Both bear ordinary adult weight. Please test before purchase rather than after returning home. Reply Box 219.

classifieds.headline: Apprentice bookbinder wanted
classifieds.body: Careful hands and willingness to learn. Applicants need not already know the trade; those who insist they do may be asked to demonstrate. Reply Box 220.

classifieds.headline: Lost: packet of family letters
classifieds.body: Tied with blue thread, no sale value. Reward for return unopened. Please leave contact details through this paper rather than print the contents. Reply Box 221.

classifieds.headline: Found: violin bow
classifieds.body: Sound stick, worn hair. Owner should identify the repair at the frog. Finder cannot play and has been asked not to continue trying. Reply Box 222.

classifieds.headline: Evening lamp repair
classifieds.body: Wicks trimmed, hinges repaired, leaking reservoirs examined. Bring an unlit lamp. This is a condition of service, not an invitation to negotiation. Reply Box 223.

classifieds.headline: Wanted: second-hand rain cloak
classifieds.body: Good fastenings more important than colour. Must keep rain on its outside for a reasonable length of time. Previous descriptions by street vendors not accepted as guarantees. Reply Box 224.

classifieds.headline: Lost: brass thimble
classifieds.body: Small thimble, worn smooth on one side. Modest reward. Please return through Box 301; it has fitted the same finger for thirty years and is missed.

classifieds.headline: Wanted: flour sacks for patching
classifieds.body: Clean empty sacks purchased or exchanged for mending. No live contents and no account of how they became empty required. Reply Box 302.

classifieds.headline: Found: a rain cloak with excellent pockets
classifieds.body: Brown cloak; owner should describe the unusual contents of the inner pocket. Finder declines to describe them first. Reply Box 303.

classifieds.headline: Lost: sketch of a cat
classifieds.body: Charcoal sketch, tabby with bell. The actual cat is safely home. Reward for return of drawing, which its young artist would like to finish. Reply Box 304.

classifieds.headline: Room available over a bakehouse
classifieds.body: Early warmth, early noise, shared water. Applicants who consider these two separate benefits preferred. Terms agreed before occupation. Reply Box 305.

classifieds.headline: Wanted: sound market basket
classifieds.body: Must carry onions without releasing them at corners. Attractive appearance optional. Please state repairs honestly; buyer owns needles. Reply Box 306.

classifieds.headline: Missing: pair of green mittens
classifieds.body: Joined by a long cord. Owner is small and the cord seems to have defeated a perfectly sound plan. Modest reward. Reply Box 307.

classifieds.headline: For sale: stout boot scraper
classifieds.body: Iron scraper with fixing holes. Seller moving to a house where the mud is already inside. Collection by arrangement. Reply Box 308.

notices.headline: Carters' notice
notices.body: Do not leave carts across doors, even doors described as seldom used. The person behind one may disagree.

notices.headline: Market reminder
notices.body: A customer's fingers are not samples. Please return them promptly and in their original number.

notices.headline: Postal reminder
notices.body: Seal parcels securely. If the contents can leave unaided, inform the counter clerk before paying.

notices.headline: Guild meeting
notices.body: Members are reminded to bring the previous minutes. Remembering approximately what happened will no longer suffice.

notices.headline: Watch notice
notices.body: Keep entrances clear during a disturbance. A crowd explaining the disturbance remains part of the obstruction.

notices.headline: Library reminder
notices.body: Books returned damp will not be accepted as newly illustrated editions.

notices.headline: Street works
notices.body: Loose paving stones reported. Please mark the stone rather than carrying it to the office as evidence.

notices.headline: Neighbourhood collection
notices.body: Donations of usable blankets welcomed. Blankets already occupied should be discussed with the occupant first.

notices.headline: Chimney sweep
notices.body: Chimneys swept by appointment. Please extinguish the fire before our arrival, rather than as a gesture of welcome.

notices.headline: Lost-property reminder
notices.body: Applicants must describe an item before viewing it. 'Mine' is not a sufficiently detailed description.

notices.headline: Wharf reminder
notices.body: Cargo labels must be attached to the cargo. A label floating beside a crate is unlikely to improve matters.

notices.headline: Public hall
notices.body: Chairs borrowed for meetings must be returned after meetings. An endless committee is not a storage agreement.

notices.headline: Allotment notice
notices.body: Competition entries must be grown by the entrant. Purchasing an unusually shaped root does not constitute cultivation.

notices.headline: Music rehearsal
notices.body: Players should agree a tune before beginning. Agreement on volume alone is no longer considered sufficient preparation.

notices.headline: Lodging notice
notices.body: Please close the street door. Keeping the weather outside is among the few services included in the rent.

notices.headline: Editorial notice
notices.body: Corrections welcomed. Please identify the incorrect sentence rather than enclosing the entire paper with the word 'all'.
