notices.headline: Notice to parcel senders
notices.body: A large word reading FRAGILE does not fasten a lid. Tie, wrap and address parcels before presenting them. Keep your own copy of any important description.

notices.headline: Rehearsal reminder
notices.body: Members of the amateur choir are asked to bring the same song to the next meeting. Enthusiasm has been adequate; agreement remains our principal difficulty.

notices.headline: Garden produce submissions
notices.body: Vegetables intended for illustration should arrive wrapped and labelled. The name of the vegetable will suffice. Elaborate explanations of what it resembles may be retained by the grower.

notices.headline: Courtyard ladder sharing
notices.body: Borrowers should return the ladder to its marked hooks. Leaving it against a different house makes the next repair both inconvenient and difficult to explain.

notices.headline: Community supper utensils
notices.body: Contributors are thanked for their spoons. The organisers now request bowls, bread and somebody willing to wash up when the applause has finished.

notices.headline: Wet paving warning
notices.body: Freshly laid stones are not improved by testing them with a cart. Please use the passage marked by the crew until the work has settled.

notices.headline: Reading circle arrangements
notices.body: Visitors may bring a book or simply listen. Loud correction of another reader's pronunciation is not a contribution to the refreshments.

notices.headline: Lost-property replies
notices.body: Reply through the numbered box unless the advertiser requests otherwise. A reward is the advertiser's offer; this paper cannot pay it on their behalf.

notices.headline: Market wrapping
notices.body: Please do not use a customer's written order as wrapping until the order has been read. Several onions recently received excellent directions and no owner.

notices.headline: Bakehouse collection
notices.body: Collect dishes by their tokens, not their smell. A convincing resemblance to supper does not settle ownership.

notices.headline: Missing animal drawings
notices.body: A useful likeness should show markings and collar details. An enormous arrow reading OUR CAT rarely helps someone who has not met it.

notices.headline: Rainy stair reminder
notices.body: Wet cloaks belong on the hooks. Laying one across the stair does not make the stair drier or the neighbour happier.

letters.headline: The matter of puddles
letters.body: Sir, the same puddle has occupied our street for a fortnight. Either repair the paving or give it a name so visitors may ask directions. — A Ratepayer

letters.headline: An economical proposal
letters.body: Sir, if guild meetings began with refreshments, members could go home sooner and save considerable candle wax. — A Concerned Treasurer

letters.headline: Regarding bells
letters.body: Sir, I welcome accurate bells, but must they all be accurate at different times? — Frequently Late

letters.headline: A correction requested
letters.body: Sir, your notice described my missing hat as brown. It is black beneath the dust. Kindly restore its dignity. — The Owner

letters.headline: About the new bench
letters.body: Sir, those complaining the bench faces the wrong way might consider sitting on the other side. I appreciate this is a radical proposal. — Practical

letters.headline: The price of string
letters.body: Sir, why is short string dearer per length than long string? I invite answers requiring no string. — Puzzled of the Market

letters.headline: A culinary distinction
letters.body: Sir, soup is a meal. Hot water near a cabbage is an intention. I trust the trade will observe this distinction. — A Paying Customer

letters.headline: On public notices
letters.body: Sir, every notice asking me not to stand here is placed exactly where I must stand to read it. — Obstructed

letters.headline: A doorstep worth keeping clear
letters.body: Sir, the delivery cart outside my shop is always described as only being there for a moment. There are so many moments that they now cover the working day. I ask merely for a gap wide enough to admit a customer. I would be grateful to discover whether the cart's owner has a shop, so that I may briefly stand in front of it. — A Shopkeeper

letters.headline: The virtue of plain instructions
letters.body: Sir, a packet marked THIS WAY UP arrived with the words on its underside. I do not blame the carrier, since two other sides bore similar instructions in different hands. Might senders agree on one top before requesting assistance? My parcel contained hats and consequently survived the debate. I should be more concerned if ordering eggs. — A Regular Correspondent

letters.headline: A sensible account of kindness
letters.body: Sir, your last issue reported a man helping his neighbour with a broken cart. I was that neighbour. He did more work than your account suggests and accepted less payment than I offered. I write because we are quick to publish complaints and remarkably slow with thanks. He will be embarrassed to read this, which I regard as fair compensation for refusing the money. — Grateful

letters.headline: A voice from the late shift
letters.body: Sir, several notices invite every worker to a meeting at noon. Some of us are asleep then because somebody must remain awake after the meeting has ended. Could the organisers occasionally ask us what time would suit, rather than announcing afterwards that nobody objected? We would object more punctually if permitted to attend while conscious. — A Night Worker

letters.headline: Respect for another person's coat
letters.body: Sir, the coat I ordered is for me. I mention this because three other customers felt entitled to advise on its colour, length and suitability before the tailor could obtain my measurements. Advice freely offered is not always freely declined. I thank the proprietor for asking which opinion came from the person paying the bill. — Finally Fitted

letters.headline: Regarding advertised rewards
letters.body: Sir, a reward ought to be an amount the owner can actually afford. After helping recover a lost trinket, I learnt that the very large reward in the notice was intended chiefly to encourage me. It has encouraged me to read more carefully. I returned the article nevertheless and request that advertisers consider what their words will mean to the finder. — Disappointed but Honest

letters.headline: An objection to prediction
letters.body: Sir, your rival predicts that all my troubles will disappear before the next issue. I respectfully point out that my landlord takes the same paper. He regards the prediction as a reason I should pay in advance. Please publish tomorrow's advice before today's debt falls due, so we may both know which arrangement to ignore. — Under a Familiar Sign

letters.headline: A gardener's modest request
letters.body: Sir, some of us grow vegetables for eating. I have produced six entirely respectable cabbages and would welcome a small mention of their excellent keeping qualities. I appreciate that this may be less exciting than another carrot with an unfortunate silhouette. Could the gardening column occasionally include a specimen that could be shown to a visiting aunt without preliminary explanation? — Quietly Productive

letters.headline: A preference for useful measurements
letters.body: Sir, I bought a measure of onions and received a debate about the size of the measure. I had planned to make soup. Could the trade supply the onions first and arrange any discussion of philosophy after the pot has boiled? — Waiting with a Spoon

letters.headline: What became of the crust
letters.body: Sir, the young apprentice mentioned in your catering correspondence is my nephew. His instructions have not always been as clear as his employer imagines. I do not claim he was right to remove the crust, merely that we should applaud his ability to keep it in one piece. — An Interested Aunt

letters.headline: An independent household member
letters.body: Sir, the cat you describe as missing has spent the afternoon asleep on my coat. I would have written sooner but did not wish to wake it. Its owner may collect it after supper, subject to negotiation with the person currently holding the coat. — Temporarily Inconvenienced

letters.headline: The dry side of the street
letters.body: Sir, my neighbour claims the opposite pavement stays drier because its residents are better organised. I invite him to make the same observation when the wind changes. I will keep a towel ready for his revised account. — Across the Way

vegetables.headline: Mr Wintler's latest submission
vegetables.body: Mr Wintler submits a carrot with what he calls a remarkable arrangement of roots. The gardening editor confirms that it grew underground and would prefer the discussion to remain there.
vegetables.alt: Black ink engraving of a knobbly carrot with two splayed roots and an awkward small central root; allotment humour

vegetables.headline: A nose for the news
vegetables.body: Mr Wintler's parsnip is reproduced at a respectful distance. He says it has a nose for a story. The editor would prefer that it acquired a taste for remaining in the garden.
vegetables.alt: Ink engraving of a parsnip with a large hooked side root resembling a comic nose

vegetables.headline: Mr Turnip, a potato
vegetables.body: Mr Wintler insists the potato is called Mr Turnip. The gardening desk pointed out the difficulty. Mr Wintler pointed out the chin, which is considerably larger.
vegetables.alt: Ink engraving of a knobbly potato with a long jutting nose and a large chin in profile

vegetables.headline: Turnip unfit for straight answers
vegetables.body: Mr Wintler's turnip came out with its root wound tighter than a watch spring. The gardening desk has ruled that it can be served as a vegetable or used to open a bottle, but preferably in that order.
vegetables.alt: Ink engraving of a round turnip with its thin root coiled like a pig's tail

vegetables.headline: Cabbage overhears everything
vegetables.body: You can tell this cabbage anything, says Mr Wintler. An hour later, the coleslaw knew.
vegetables.alt: Ink engraving of a cabbage with two large outer leaves shaped like ears

vegetables.headline: Leek ties itself in knots
vegetables.body: The knot has been inspected by two sailors and a gardener. The sailors can tell us what it is. The gardener is the only one willing to untie it.
vegetables.alt: Ink engraving of a leek with its long green blades twisted into a large knot

vegetables.headline: An onion with spectacles
vegetables.body: Mr Wintler says the spectacles grew with the onion. Our gardening correspondent tried them on and found they made everything very blurry, principally because he was crying.
vegetables.alt: Ink engraving of an onion with two large rings of dry skin shaped like spectacles

vegetables.headline: Beetroot banned from the front row
vegetables.body: Mr Wintler's beetroot has been invited to audition at the Opera House. The management asks that it keep its roots below shoulder height until the other dancers have gone home.
vegetables.alt: Ink engraving of a beetroot with two crooked roots raised in a high kick

vegetables.headline: Celery gives directions
vegetables.body: The celery points firmly towards the tram stop, which the city does not have. Three people have followed it all the same. One has bought a season ticket.
vegetables.alt: Ink engraving of a celery bunch with its stalks growing into a pointing shape

vegetables.headline: Cucumber applies to join the Watch
vegetables.body: Sergeant Colon says the moustache is more than adequate. He is waiting to see what the rest of the applicant looks like.
vegetables.alt: Ink engraving of a bumpy cucumber grown in the shape of a handlebar moustache

vegetables.headline: Pea exceeds its allowance
vegetables.body: There were six peas in the pod, says Mr Wintler. The smallest five dispute this and say there was one pea and a housing shortage.
vegetables.alt: Ink engraving of an open pea pod with small peas crowded around one oversized pea

vegetables.headline: Pumpkin takes two seats
vegetables.body: Mr Wintler's pumpkin took the prize for size and most of the bench. We thank the judges for conducting the remainder of the judging standing up.
vegetables.alt: Ink engraving of a squat ribbed pumpkin with two round lobes and a deep central crease
